claims.text: SECTION 2a PROVENANCE, THE DIVERGENCE. The two accounts agree on substance and diverge on posture and agency. Johnson's account is passive throughout, frozen to the steering wheel, unable to speak or blink, hearing Woods shouting; Woods's is active, out of the truck and calling Johnson to come and look. Agreement on substance with divergence on detail reads very differently from verbatim agreement, and it is the strongest thing in the second account's favour.

claims.text: The episode's own corroboration claim is narrow and explicit: a three-word instruction not to fear, asserted at 01:17:08-01:17:27 to have been produced by two men in two rooms hours apart. Johnson produced the phrase in waking conversation at 00:20:26, before his regression, which is better ordering than the narration's own framing suggests. Against it: the phrase is a staple of the abduction literature and of Woods's own published accounts since 1996, and the episode does not establish that Johnson had not encountered them.

conflicts: The durations are mutually inconsistent inside one episode: nine hours in the description, five in the narration at 00:01:02, five and a half at 00:55:39. The elapsed-year figures likewise: fifty, forty-nine and forty-eight and a half.
The narration's 'massive glowing red orb' matches neither claimant's waking description, which are 'big' and 'white'.
The episode's on-camera account of the moment of recognition contradicts its own recording of that moment.

desc: A CLAIM WITH NO AIR FORCE RECORD BEHIND IT, ADMITTED UNDER CLAUDE.md SECTION 2a AND GRADED AT TIER 2. The account is that on 18 November 1977 at about 0100, on an 1800 to 0600 shift, two United States Air Force security policemen of the 44th Missile Security Squadron responded to an alarm at Launch Facility November-5 in the Ellsworth AFB Minuteman field; that a large bright object hovered under about fifty feet above the site; that four humanoid figures approached the truck; that both men were taken aboard and physically examined; that hours were lost; and that both were recovered about eight miles away beside a reservoir dam, one of them catatonic at the wheel, and interrogated separately on base. NO AIR FORCE RECORD OF THE EVENT HAS EVER BEEN PRODUCED BY ANY PARTY AND NO SERVICE RECORD FOR EITHER MAN HAS BEEN OPENED BY THIS BOARD. What is dated is the telling, and the two tellings have opposite provenance: Mario Woods has given the account publicly since 1996 and named his partner on air for years; Michael Johnson was located by the publishing party on 26 June 2026 from a viewer's tip and has no dated pre-contact statement about the event of any kind. The node carries the discovery chain, the prompt on the recorded call and the divergence between the two accounts, because under section 2a those are part of the claim and not commentary on it.
